author: abeltre1
tooling: Patched image built from Dockerfile in this directory; evidence gathered by image inspection, ELF linkage analysis, and runtime library mapping; see README.md

vulnerability.name: CVE-2025-15367
vulnerability.description: cpython poplib command injection via newlines in user-controlled POP3 commands

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in the poplib module and is only reachable when an application passes user-controlled strings to POP3 commands. No module in the image's virtual environment imports poplib, and LiteLLM does not speak POP3, so the vulnerable code is never executed. No fixed CPython release exists; the image's Python is the current head of the 3.13 branch (commit 15e701a)

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-12345
vulnerability.description: cpython tempfile.TemporaryDirectory cleanup race allowing deletion outside the directory via symlink swap

statements.impact_statement: Exploitation requires an attacker who can modify the temporary directory tree while it is being removed. TemporaryDirectory creates its directory with mkdtemp, mode 0700, owned by the process user, so only that user (uid 65534) or root can change it. The container runs a single workload as uid 65534 and does not share its temporary directory with other users. LiteLLM's own uses stage files the proxy itself writes; skill code runs in a separate sandbox container and cannot reach the proxy's temporary directories. No fixed CPython release exists

alsa-lib remains only in the arm64 image, where the system libsndfile must stay because the soundfile wheel for arm64 does not bundle its own copy; on amd64 the Dockerfile removes libsndfile and alsa-lib with it. libasound.so.2 is linked only by /usr/bin/sndfile-play, /usr/bin/aserver, and /usr/lib/libatopology.so, none of which the proxy executes or loads. libsndfile.so.1, the library soundfile loads on arm64, links only libm, libogg, libvorbis, libvorbisenc, libFLAC, libopus, libc, and the loader, so audio handling never loads alsa-lib
